description: Per-event dispatcher manifest. Each event lists the SESSION-NEW checks consolidated behind one hook invocation. dispatch.py reads stdin once, runs each check whose `matcher` (regex on tool_name; absent = always) matches, IN-PROCESS in its own thread with a per-check timeout, fail-open, and aggregates every check's additionalContext into ONE hookSpecificOutput for the event. Adding a future check = one line here (seeds the later Discipline-Forge). The PRE-EXISTING B1/legacy hooks are intentionally NOT listed here and stay as their own settings.json entries.

SessionStart.rebalance_note: 2026-08-27 wave A-c (CONSOLIDATED-GEM-DECISIONS TIER-0 #2): wire-check and git-hygiene DEMOTED here from Stop, whose 35s ceiling starved the tail gates (journey-coverage, dark-surface). Both are advisory/inject-only and git-hygiene self-throttles to one scan/15min, so once-per-session is the right cadence. settings_timeout raised 20->35 IN LOCKSTEP with the live settings.json SessionStart dispatch entry (same edit) so the moved checks' 25s/30s budgets stay reachable -- a budget above the enforced ceiling is inert (see git-hygiene timeout_rationale). ARITHMETIC CORRECTION (2026-09-29, L1): the original note read 'oversubscribed (9 checks, timeouts summing 144s)', reasoning from timeouts SUMMING. That MECHANISM is wrong: dispatch.py runs checks CONCURRENTLY -- :351-358 starts every thread before the single shared start = time.monotonic() at :360, and :362-372 joins against absolute deadlines -- so the governing quantity is max(timeout), NOT the sum (empirically confirmed: 3 checks x 6s at timeouts 10/8/30 finished in 6.01s, not 18s). Current SessionStart = 8 checks, sum 103s but max 30s (git-hygiene) against the 35s ceiling, with a measured serial-import phase of only 0.084s, so ~5s of genuine collection headroom -- exactly the 5s this note already claims. The 144s figure was the true SUM of the old 9-check Stop set (89+25+30) but described a cost model the dispatcher does not implement; the historical 90s-on-Stop incident it cites was a MAX-exceeds-ceiling failure (a single 90s budget held run() past the 35s cancellation point, so the vendor killed the whole dispatcher and lost all Stop checks' output), NOT a sum failure -- git-hygiene timeout_rationale below already documents this absolute-deadline/max model. Consequently the L1 mcp-liveness/sessionstart check above (timeout 8) costs zero wall clock: 8 < max 30, nothing is demoted, shrunk, or gated.

checks.name: mcp-liveness/sessionstart
checks.comment: L1. liveness.py:9 ('SessionStart -> always probe basic-memory (the resume-after-hours case)') and :44 ('python liveness.py sessionstart # SessionStart hook') document this route; it was never registered, so the sessionstart-only always-alert branch at :456-457 was DEAD CODE. The pretool route (events.PreToolUse, matcher mcp__basic-memory__.*) cannot substitute: when basic-memory is down the MCP server fails to connect and its tools are ABSENT from the session, so no mcp__basic-memory__* call can be issued and the only route to the restart is removed by the very outage it detects. Measured: ~/.basic-memory/logs/liveness-restart.log did not exist at all until the helper was invoked by hand. heartbeat (already at SessionStart) is NOT a substitute - heartbeat.py:119-131 is a bare 0.4s TCP connect and :124 explicitly defers the handshake to the PreToolUse hook, so SessionStart had detection without remediation. isolate is null (liveness.py imports no _common/stubscan sibling). side_effect is NOT 'none': it writes per-session state via save_state() and may spawn the restart helper. Inject-only and fail-open: run() returns 0 on every path (:454-472) and speaks solely through emit(). Opt-out: hooks/mcp-liveness/.disabled.
checks.timeout_rationale: 8 = measured worst case + margin. critical.json bounds the probe at handshake_timeout 5.0 + tcp_timeout 1.5 = 6.5s. Measured DOWN-state cost 1.640-1.654s cold over three runs of the read-only 'probe' mode (tcp_timeout dominates; probe_reharness adds nothing because the re-harness registry.json does not exist). The restart is fire-and-forget - attempt_restart uses subprocess.Popen with no .wait() (:343-351) - so it contributes zero blocking time. Costs ZERO additional wall clock: dispatch.py:351-372 runs checks CONCURRENTLY against absolute deadlines from one shared start, so the batch wall clock is max(timeout)=30 (git-hygiene), not the sum; 8 < 30.

checks.name: git-hygiene
checks.comment: Moved from Stop 2026-08-27 (wave A-c) -- see SessionStart.rebalance_note. Surfaces live-authored harness artifacts (skills/hooks/rules under ~/.claude,~/.agents) not yet in agent-skills-toolchain, plus your repos holding unversioned work. Self-throttles to one full scan per 15 min (GIT_HYGIENE_THROTTLE_SEC). Advisory/inject, never blocks. Opt-out: GIT_HYGIENE=off or hooks/git-hygiene/.disabled.
checks.timeout_rationale: 30 leaves 5s of collection headroom under the (raised) 35s SessionStart ceiling -- same headroom pattern the Stop event used. History: was 90 on Stop, which was UNREACHABLE (Stop ceiling 35s; dispatch.py collects with an absolute deadline of start+timeout, so a 90s budget held run() past the cancellation point and the vendor killed the whole dispatcher command, losing all 9 Stop checks' output -- proved by _b12_joinorder.py). Measured range 11.8-32.7s (R4-GITHYGIENE-RANGE.json): runs above 30s lose THIS check's output only, an acceptable trade for an advisory/inject-only check.

checks.name: dark-surface
checks.comment: A6 wire-dormant-gates. dark-surface/check.py:13-14 already documents 'this is the mode the session-new _dispatch/manifest.json runs it under', but the entry was never actually added -- the GREEN-not-LIVE defect the gate itself exists to catch. stub-ledger/report.py:258 returns 0 on a completion-claim Stop turn to 'defer to dark-surface', so while this was unwired NEITHER gate fired on exactly the turns that matter. Shadow/observe-only by default (DARK_SURFACE_MODE=shadow), inject-only, never blocks, fail-open. side_effect is 'shadow-sink' not 'none' because it appends to ~/.agents/state/harness/shadow/shadow-<day>.jsonl (check.py:115-145); the neighbouring side_effect='none' checks write nothing. Opt-out: DARK_SURFACE=off or hooks/dark-surface/.disabled.

checks.name: claim-guard/ledger-write
checks.comment: D011 producer-restore. The Bash-exit ledger this hook appends (%TEMP%/claude-claim-ledger/<sid>.ndjson, ledger-write.py:15,195-197) is NOT an orphan surface: journey-coverage/check.py:36-41 reads exactly that root and is ALREADY wired under events.Stop.checks, so while this producer was absent the live consumer ran every Stop turn against an empty ledger and could never see a journey as covered. Contract mirrors test_wiring.py:140 (args [], matcher Bash, timeout 5, emits false) -- record-only, injects nothing (ledger-write.py:10), fail-open (:199-200), opt-out CLAIM_GUARD_MODE=off (:165-166). Restoring the WRITER only is deliberate: claim-check.py can exit 2 under CLAIM_GUARD_MODE=block (claim-check.py:22-24,36-37) and must therefore stay OUT of the inject-only dispatcher.

checks.name: edit-validate/record
checks.comment: The missing PRODUCER for the Stop gate wired above. dark-surface/check.py:190-202 reads <temp>/edit-validate/<session_id>.edits and returns [] on any missing file, so :217-230 found nothing to scan on every turn -- the Stop entry was live but permanently inert. record.py:19-40 is its sole producer and was registered in no surface; stub-ledger/report.py returns 0 on a completion-claim Stop turn to 'defer to dark-surface', so while this was unwired NEITHER half fired on exactly the turns that matter. This is the same GREEN-not-LIVE defect the dark-surface entry was itself added to catch, one layer down. Route pinned by test_wiring.EXPECTED_DISPATCH_ROUTES (args [], matcher Edit|Write|MultiEdit, timeout 5, emits false); presence + route asserted by test_manifest_presence.py. isolate is null because record.py imports no _common/stubscan sibling. side_effect is 'edits-append' not 'none': it appends one line per edit to <temp>/edit-validate/<sid>.edits (record.py:35-40). It NEVER emits and never wakes Claude -- that loop-proofing is the whole point of the design (record.py:5-8).

PreToolUse.settings_matcher_drift: 2026-09-29, L1 (NOTE ONLY -- settings.json is not this unit's file). The settings_matcher declared above does NOT match the LIVE ~/.claude/settings.json PreToolUse dispatch entry. Declared here: 'Task|Edit|Write|MultiEdit|mcp__basic-memory__.*|Workflow|mcp__codex__codex|Bash|PowerShell'. LIVE (verified this session by parsing settings.json): 'Agent|Task|Write|mcp__basic-memory__write_note|mcp__basic-memory__edit_note|Workflow|mcp__codex__codex|Bash|PowerShell'. Because the live outer wire is the ENFORCED one, two consequences: (1) the mcp-liveness/pretool check's inner matcher mcp__basic-memory__.* can only ever see write_note/edit_note -- the live outer wire admits only those two basic-memory tools, so a recall call (search_notes/build_context/recent_activity) never reaches the dispatcher even with the server UP; that is why the L1 mcp-liveness/sessionstart route added to SessionStart is the only always-on remediation path. (2) edit-checkpoints (inner matcher Edit|Write|MultiEdit) is reachable only on Write, because the live outer wire omits Edit|MultiEdit -- so the /rollback producer whose comment at the edit-checkpoints entry claims 'settings_matcher gained Edit|MultiEdit so the outer wire actually reaches this route' is live for ONE of its three tools. This records the drift and hands the orchestrator a scoped settings.json follow-up (align the live matcher to this declared value, or narrow this declared value to the live one) rather than leaving a false reachability claim unrecorded in the manifest.

checks.name: edit-checkpoints
checks.comment: The PRODUCER for /rollback. commands/rollback.md:3-7 promises a checkpoint is taken automatically before edits and :21-24 reads ~/.claude/checkpoints/<session_id>/index.ndjson, but checkpoint.py was registered in NO surface -- not here, not hooks.json -- so a fresh session had no index to roll back to. Dispatcher-compatible: checkpoint.py:17 is silent and inject-free, main() returns 0 on every path and fail-opens on any exception, so it adds no blocking or emitting behaviour. Route pinned by test_wiring.py EXPECTED_DISPATCH_ROUTES['PreToolUse']['edit-checkpoints'] = ([], 'Edit|Write|MultiEdit', 15, False). settings_matcher gained Edit|MultiEdit so the outer wire actually reaches this route (agent-self/config/settings.json already routes all three). Opt-out: EDIT_CHECKPOINTS=off or hooks/edit-checkpoints/.disabled.
